Arrow to the heart: Bunnies and Roosters set to unite for Jai
They’ve been at each other for 118 years but on Friday night hostilities will cease for a few minutes as players and fans from South Sydney Rabbitohs and Sydney Roosters honour Jai Arrow in his 100th NRL game.
Following on from the emotional celebrations at Cbus Stadium last week for Arrow’s 99th game, another packed house at Allianz Stadium will continue that love for the 31-year-old for his 100th.
"Over the weekend, even since the announcement of Jai's condition, we've seen that some things are bigger than football,” said Roosters utility Connor Watson.
"He's obviously going to play his 100th game for the Rabbitohs on Friday so we'll be there to celebrate with him.”
Arrow’s MND diagnosis has brought all corners of the game together to offer support and love for the Arrow family.
“There's a lot of things in the game of rugby league we can't change,” said Roosters prop Naufahu Whyte.
“I send my full love and respect out to Jai and his family and what he's done for the game.
In full: Jai Arrow's return to the pitch
"It's a privilege to be in that moment with him as he represents his 100th game.
"I know all us Roosters brothers support him.”
Both Watson and Whyte said there would be no issue balancing the acknowledgement for Arrow with the need to then go out and play 80 minutes of high intensity footy against a fellow finalist.
"It's all a mindset,” Whyte said.
“One moment you can be in a situation and another moment you can flick that switch in your head and go into battle.
Bennett talks about the love for Jai Arrow
"We'll celebrate that moment with Jai - he deserves it - and then we'll cross those white lines and get ready for the match.”
Whyte has a 4-2 record against Souths since his first ‘Book of Feuds’ experience in Round 24, 2021.
In 2026 he’s looking forward to the up-front confrontation with Tevita Tatola and Keaon Koloamatangi.
“Most definitely... obviously the history but also the energy you get against the Bunnies, everyone is hunting, it's a full 80-minute game with no change in tempo or intensity," Whyte said.
“That's what makes the rivalry so special. I'm grateful to be part of it.”
Whyte dismisses the recent Roosters losses against Wests Tigers (Round 25) and Dolphins (Round 26) as harming team confidence in any way.
"We're not worried at all about it. It's part of the journey, part of the season,” he said.

"Every good team, every great team, has had their downfalls. I guess we're riding that now but I still have full belief.
"I still back my brothers and know what we're capable of doing.
"What is said within these four walls is sacred to us - the belief is high.
“These two losses don't rattle us at all.
"We've taken our lessons over the past couple of weeks and we head into this game with a new fresh mindset - we're going after it.”

items.body_excerpt:
Every year, as we run into the final round of the season, the same old question gets trotted out.
Should top teams rest their stars to be fresh for the finals?
Resting has become almost an epidemic in previous years, and with the top two, the next two, and then the top eight locked in bar some small positional changes, it was thought there could have been plenty this go around.
But Tuesday afternoon's team lists didn't exactly bring a lot in the way of resting, until you got to the Sydney Roosters .
James Tedesco , Billy Smith , Robert Toia , Mark Nawaqanitawase , Daly Cherry-Evans , Hugo Savala , Naufahu Whyte , Reece Robson , Nat Butcher and Siua Wong have all been rested.
Sam Walker is also olut injured, so from last week's run on side who were easily beaten by the Dolphins , Robinson has just two players left, with Lindsay Collins to skipper the side from prop, and Salesi Foketi , who has been excellent on the edge in recent weeks but will likely lose his starting spot to a returning Angus Crichton in the finals, in the side.
It does present opportunity for a number of Roosters young guns to fire, while Daniel Tupou will return from injury in a much-needed hit out before the finals roll around.
SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 05: Daniel Tupou of the Roosters scores a try during the round 27 NRL match between the Sydney Roosters and South Sydney Rabbitohs at Allianz Stadium on September 05, 2025, in Sydney, Australia. (Photo by Cameron Spencer/Getty Images)
Resting is something that divides opinion, and while personally, it's hard to have a problem with it, it is easy to question exactly what the Roosters are doing this weekend.
The great resting debate reared its head last year when the Canberra Raiders did it.
Ricky Stuart's team won the minor premiership with a week to spare, got flogged by the Dolphins on the last day of the season, and went on to be knocked out in straight sets.
That, in a nutshell, is the risk of the rest.
It has worked for other teams, namely the Penrith Panthers , over the years, but it's difficult to suggest it's the right reign to pull when your team is down on their form.
That's exactly where the tri-colours find themselves heading into the finals.
Robinson's side have lost their last two games, and while last weekend's slip up against the Dolphins could potentially be excused given the Redcliffe-based side are also sitting pretty in the top four, the fact it came a week after they fell short against the rabble that has become the Wests Tigers needs serious investigation.
The Roosters form tailing off at the wrong end of the season was probably a reason to play most of their stars this weekend, maybe with the exception of guys who were involved in State of Origin , or have had signiifcant minutes across the course of the campaign.
What it wasn't a reason to do was rest everybody.
Form is just one part of the equation for the Roosters.
The fact they are playing arch-rivals the South Sydney Rabbitohs in the final round gives the Maroubra-based outfit a chance to put a serious score on the tri-colours, picking up their own momentum and raising questions of the Roosters.
But it's two other big factors which should be raising eyebrows.

Lindsay Collins has spent a decade leading by example at the Roosters. On Friday night he’ll officially lead them out for the first time.
With James Tedesco and second-choice skipper Daly Cherry-Evans among nine players rested ahead of the finals, Roosters coach Trent Robinson has handed Collins the captaincy duties for Friday's clash with South Sydney.
The prop has steadily developed into a leader within the Roosters squad throughout the past few years and Robinson said it was a special moment telling the Queensland and Australian representative he would be leading the side.

“He’s been our vice-captain for a while there; he’s been a leader in this club for many, many years and it’s his first captaincy, so that was a really nice moment to talk to him about leading the team out,” Robinson said.

items.body_excerpt:
It's the little things that count for high-flying Roosters: Kelly
Roosters gun Isabelle Kelly has heaped praise on master mentor John Strange and her middle forwards as the backbone of the club’s stunning charge towards a third NRLW premiership.
Win No.9 came at the expense of the Sharks 36-8 at Allianz Stadium with only the Cowboys in Townsville and Bulldogs back at Allianz left to complete an historic unbeaten season.
Six of the seven tries against the Sharks were scored by outside backs, including two to Brydie Parker in her 50th game, but Kelly is adamant the 9-0 run is a tribute to every player who has donned the famous jersey in 2026.
“Really proud to be honest, finding little things where we can be a lot better,” Kelly told NRL.com.
"Defence has been our biggest focus with that. Also, really proud of the girls that don't get mentioned, our middle pack.
“Those girls are really paving the platform for all of us to be able to go out and dominate.
“There are a lot of our players that don't get recognition, they push week in and week out, and tonight they did again.”
Chief in her thoughts would have been props Millie Elliott with 78 post-contact metres and Otesa Pule with 50 post-contact and two tackle breaks.
Brydie Parker with two special tries
Hooker Keeley Nizza topped the tackle count for both sides with 39 while lock Olivia Kernick ran for 103 metres and made 30 tackles.
And pulling the talent together is coach Strange, who has won the past two Origin series with NSW along with two NRLW premierships with the Roosters (2021 and 2024).
“I could talk for hours about Strangey and his professionalism, his ability to bring confidence and shine on everyone’s best attributes,” said Kelly.
Jessica Sergis in the tries
“They might have a bad game but he shines on the good things.
“He is one of the best if not the best.... what he does in the women’s space, is amazing and what he pushes towards.”
After eight seasons with the Roosters, Kelly continues to get a buzz out of the support of the club's fans.
“I have been at the club for a long time, the fan loyalty stands out for me, they are so loyal to women’s game and our team,” said Kelly.
“They really have been with us through the highs and lows, losing grand finals, they were riding with us.
“And the club's support of the women's program is amazing.
"With the right staff, especially with Strangey, it’s incredible. I’m super proud. I will be here for life.”

Sydney Roosters coach Trent Robinson has given an update on his injured star halfback Sam Walker .
Walker went down with a syndesmosis injury last weekend in the tri-colours' loss to the Dolphins after his ankle became trapped awkwardly under a defender.
He was quickly aided off the field and underwent surgery on Sunday, with Robinson hoping to get him on the field "as soon as possible".
It is a massive blow to the Roosters' premiership muscle, and they will rely on Daly Cherry-Evans and Hugo Savala to gel for their finals series, which they are expected to go deep into.
The Roosters provided a statement following Walker's surgery, saying he will undergo an intense rehabilitation process in an attempt to get him back playing before the end of the season.
Robinson remains hopeful the Maroons star halfback can return and help deliver a trophy in Bondi for the first time in seven years.
“He got operated on on Sunday afternoon. There's not much to do in the initial sort of phase of recovery there, and then he'll get going pretty quickly. They heal quite quickly those injuries," Robinson said to media on Thursday.
It is fortunate the Roosters can rely on 370-game veteran Daly Cherry-Evans to slide into his preferred halfback position, where he boasts plenty of big-game experience in finals and State of Origin .
Although Robinson is hopeful to return to their similar halves pairing in time before the first weekend of October, if the Roosters' season is still alive.
“There are some pretty clear signposts along the way about games and stuff like that around what's possible," he added.
SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA - MARCH 17: Sam Walker of the Roosters kicks during the round two NRL match between Manly Sea Eagles and Sydney Roosters at 4 Pines Park, on March 17, 2024, in Sydney, Australia. (Photo by Cameron Spencer/Getty Images)
"We just need to push it as far as he can handle it and see where we get to.”
The Roosters will face arch rivals South Sydney on Friday night, in what is historically a blockbuster fixture.
Although the club has rested a bunch of stars, including Cherry-Evans, Reece Robson , Mark Nawaqanitawase, Suia Wong, Robert Toia , and skipper James Tedesco , to give his key personnel a rest before the intense finals matches begin.
He declared it was "the best thing for the club" in their push for the trophy in 2026, and with a top four position already secured, they can take the gamble if it means his stars are fresh for Week 1.
"The scenario was pretty clear that we were third or fourth, and then trying to pick what was going to happen in one and two… it was all really clear what was the best thing for us this week and what players had played either Origin or a fair amount of time leading up to that game,” he said.
Although Robinson believes the inexperienced team can still do a job on the Rabbitohs, who will play elimination play-offs next weekend.
“That was the clear point, and we have clear belief in what we can achieve tomorrow night with the team. They're all Roosters players, they've been in our system for a long time. We're also really clear about the following week as well.”

As it happened: Knights strike back; Roosters undefeated, Titans go eight straight
The Titans kicked off Saturday's NRLW action by taking down the Raiders 26-20 in an entertaining contest at Cbus Super Stadium.
The two sides were hard to split for much of the first half until the Lauren Brown show really kicked off, orchestrating three tries in seven minutes leading into half-time to put the Titans in front 18-6.
The Titans marched on in the second half and the lead blew out to 26-6, but the Raiders were not going to let it end there, scoring three late tries to close the gap, with Mackenzie Wiki finishing with a hat-trick including a remarkable team try after the full-time siren.
It was the eight straight win for the Titans and solidifies them in second position on the ladder.
In the second game, the Roosters made it nine in a row against a Sharks outfit enduring a horror injury run. They were unfortunately struck again in the game with forward Rhiannon Byers suffering a knee injury in their 36-8 loss.
The final instalment of our Saturday triple took us to Townsville where the Cowboys were looking to continue a late charge that had seen them win three of their past four matches to climb from last on the ladder to ninth.
However, the visiting Newcastle proved far too strong, overpowering the home side with a dominant 40-6 win, putting them back on track after a string of losses had seem them in danger of missing the finals for the first time since their inaugural season in 2021.
